title: Project Runpi Initial Launch
overview: My site has been completely rebuilt from the ground up, with both the backend and frontend refactored to make everything more scalable and maintainable.
content:
What’s New in This Overhaul

This release isn't just a small update. it's a complete transformation of the entire website, touching everything from the design to the backend architecture and frontend structure.

Changes

  • Backend is now modular

  • Frontend now uses a mono-repo

  • Adding Filament for admin dashboard

Backend

It's now using a modular. meaning all subdomains are rested in its own dir. it has its own controller, model, migration config and routes. the backend also refactors to streamline everything. adding a command to make a controller and model to the domain module. Adding Filament (dashboard) make things easier. this devlog was posted/made inside filament.

Frontend

making front end to use mono-repo is not an easy task. I encounter a lot of problem in its and PnP itself. but I manage to solve each problem. my fronted use one PnP that uses by all mono-repo. also, Typescript suddenly works by using this setup. Now I can just add new project and develop normally. React now serve as a container. Every data comes form the backend (will not it all), but most data that I want to change on the fly

Server

I also overhaul the server. from directory to sorting files, data and container. Deploying is also now easy. I'm using shell script to deploy my website with rollback in mind. I'm planning to make this more streamline, but for now it is working the way I want.

title: Devlog adjustment
content:
Count View

Adjusted how view counts increment. Still tracked in the controller but added session to prevent duplicates.

Tag Color

Adding sequential color cycling to tags, same thing done on the homepage.

Log Sorting

Sort logs from the latest.

Title and Meta Description

The title and description weren't updating with the previous setup. To maintain Google SEO indexing, I'm using useEffect() to force updates on the client side.

title: Project RunPi is in Production
overview: Just a quick update that Project RunPi is now running in production after a complete rebuild of both the backend and frontend.
content:
Hey everyone,

Project RunPi is now in production. After rebuilding everything from scratch to make it more scalable and maintainable, it's finally up and running.

What is Project RunPi? It's my portfolio homepage where I keep all the apps and projects I've built. Pretty much just a central place to see what I'm working on and what I've worked on before.

The rebuild was mostly about cleaning up the codebase and making sure things actually work properly long-term. The old version was getting a bit messy to maintain, so I took the time to do it right this time. Both the backend and frontend got refactored, which should make adding new stuff way easier going forward.

What's next? Nothing too crazy, just the usual:

  • Adding new projects when I build them

  • Tweaking things based on how it's performing

  • Maybe some new features if I feel like it

I'll probably be updating it as I work on new things, so it'll grow over time. For now, it does what it needs to do.

That's about it. If you want to check out what I've been building, it's there.

title: Project RunPi MC Server Info Page
overview: Built a server info page for the Project RunPi Minecraft server. The page shows live server status, player count, and all the important details players need before joining, like the MC version, modloader, and current modpack.
content:
Page for monitoring


I developed this page to monitor and also share my current Minecraft server
that is also running on a Raspberry Pi 5.

The backend uses xPaw/PHP-Minecraft-Query. I use MinecraftPing instead of
Query since my default container is running on TCP. Turns out the regular
Ping already returns everything needed, Like players online, max slots, version,
description, and even the server favicon as base64.

On the frontend, server data is passed directly as an Inertia prop instead of
fetching it on the client side. Decided against polling every few seconds since
it's a server info page. since nobody's sitting there waiting for the player count
to change in real time.

One thing to clean up later. The ping returns a sample list and I'm not sure
if it will show all 8 players, so decided to skip showing individual player
names for now.

STILL LEFT TO DO

  • Hook up real server IP and Dynmap URL

  • Decide whether to show the player list or not

title: Project Card
overview: Refactored the Project Card component. Updated the object structure and changed how the card handles its props.
content:
Changes how Project Cards are display


Before, the project card was using conditions and mapping to render stuff. Now I just pass the parameters directly, so no more mapping. This way I can easily control what elements and styles show up based on the props passed in.

title: Building My Deployment Pipeline
overview: I set up Gitea and Jenkins to manage my deployment pipeline. Gitea is public for showcasing repositories, while Jenkins runs internally to handle automation.
content:
Gitea

I use Gitea and self-hosted it. this is where I put all of my codes. this is also where my repository will be showcase. another thing is I need this one for Jenkin for Deployment pipeline automation. one single push to the repo and it will deploy itself.

Jenkins

I found Jenkin few days ago. i search what is Jenkins and to my surprise this is what I'm looking for. now whenever I push something on my repo. it will start to read the script and deploy my web app.

The error I encounter

I got many error. it's not due to the setup. but for on the Jenkins script. also, it was really hard to think what directory I should mount since it was running inside container. but after multiple tries. the deployment pipelines are ready to use

title: Yarn to pnpm SSR and Cross Device HMR
overview: Switched frontend tooling from Yarn to pnpm for better performance. Added Inertia SSR support and got HMR working across both PC and mobile via ZeroTier.
content:
After a month of no posts, I made a lot of changes to my frontend React tooling.

Yarn to pnpm

The first change was migrating from Yarn to pnpm for faster installs, better monorepo support, and cleaner node_modules management overall.

SSR

Next, I added Inertia SSR (Server-Side Rendering) to improve initial load performance and properly prepare the app for production. This also improves SEO and Google indexing since pages are now rendered server-side instead of relying purely on client-side JavaScript.

HMR

Finally, the most satisfying part was getting HMR (Hot Module Replacement) working across all devices. With wireless debugging enabled, I can now build a much more refined mobile-first UI. Any code change reflects instantly on both PC and mobile through ZeroTier, with no extra configuration needed per device.

Note: My current portfolio still needs some refactoring to fully support SSR, but that’s a task for another day.

title: Devlog View Count Adjustment
overview: Refactor how view count is handle
content:
Log View Count

Refactor how log vie count is increment. old way was increment on view URL.
This one has a lot of issues, like reloading or visiting the log view page will increment the view.
BOT Crawler can easily trigger the view count.


View Increment on click

I used onClick for more raw view count. this way visiting the page URL won't trigger the view increment.
This also prevent BOT Crawler to trigger it.

Only way to trigger the view increment is by clicking the URL.

I know that this is not perfect, and I might change it again once I learn a most effective ways
